what: main() issues a single {cmd:"status"} (and later a single {cmd:"actions"}) immediately after connect and asserts framesObserved>0, lastFrameHadProjection===true and >=1 attached action set off that one snapshot, with no retry/poll.
why_meaningless: Nothing waits for the app to reach a rendering/attached state; it is a one-shot read of whatever state exists at that instant, so a slow-but-healthy app is reported as a defect.
impact: Observed, tracked defect: .claude/harness/backlog.md 'Open — 実エンジンアプリ E2E から出た課題 (2026-07-25) / [P3] hello-xr-e2e-status-race' records a real run with frames=0/sets=0 producing 6 FAILs and rc=2, with a clean 20/20 on re-run. False-red on a supposedly deterministic E2E gate; repeated flakes train reviewers to dismiss red runs.
fix: Wrap the baseline probe in a bounded retry loop (mirror the SESSION_WAIT_MS pattern in scripts/vrdevapp_client.mjs:69-78): poll status until framesObserved>0 && lastFrameHadProjection===true, and poll actions until >=1 attached set, before running the asserts. Fail explicitly (with the last snapshot) on deadline so a genuinely dead app still goes red.
evidence: scripts/integration_hello_xr.mjs:150-168 — `const st = await rpc({cmd:"status"}); ... check("projection frames flowing", (cap.framesObserved||0)>0 && cap.lastFrameHadProjection===true, ...)` then `const act = await rpc({cmd:"actions"})`, both single-shot. Wrapper: scripts/integration_test.sh:60-71 waits only for a TCP LISTEN then `sleep 6`.
verify_note: Tried to reject on the theory that integration_test.sh already gates on real readiness — it does not. scripts/integration_test.sh:60 comments 'Wait for the layer control channel to LISTEN on 52700 (session reached FOCUSED)', but layer/src/layer_entry.cpp:234 calls ControlChannelStart() inside xrCreateApiLayerInstance, i.e. at INSTANCE creation, before any session/swapchain/frame exists (scripts/vrdevapp_client.mjs:66-68 states this correctly). So LISTEN + a fixed `sleep 6` is the entire readiness margin, and CaptureStatusJson() (layer/src/capture.cpp:584-601) returns framesObserved=0 / empty swapchains until the app actually renders. The wrapper comment is itself stale/wrong. Empirically reproduced and logged by the project on 2026-07-25. CONFIRMED.

what: CaptureOnCreateSwapchain stores createInfo->arraySize into SwapchainInfo (line 293), but no code path ever compares it against the app-supplied view.arrayIndex / view.depthArrayIndex before dispatching to a backend. capture.cpp is the only place both values coexist, and it is the only place the Vulkan backend's gap can be closed at all.
why_meaningless: The stored field never performs the correctness job its presence implies. Note the candidate's 'ignored-input' framing is only half right: the field IS read (CaptureStatusJson, line 591) and that JSON is consumed downstream (scripts/integration_hello_xr.mjs:157 `const sc = (cap.swapchains && cap.swapchains[0]) || {}`, used at :225 for sc.height), so it is live diagnostics, not dead storage. The real defect is the missing cross-check, not an unused field.
impact: Same silently-broken-image class as candidate 2, but this is the only site that can fix the Vulkan path: 2 of 3 graphics backends (Vulkan, D3D11) accept an out-of-range array index end-to-end while D3D12 rejects it, so identical malformed input yields {ok:false} on D3D12 and {ok:true}+garbage PNG on the other two. For Vulkan an out-of-range baseArrayLayer is undefined behaviour (crash or wrong layer), not merely a dropped copy.
fix: In capture.cpp, before `be->readback(...)` at :452 and :533 (and before ResolveDepth for view.depthArrayIndex), look up g_swapchains[view.swapchain].arraySize and return the existing explicit-error JSON shape when view.arrayIndex >= arraySize. That single fix covers Vulkan + D3D11 and makes capture_d3d12.cpp:159-162 a redundant belt-and-braces check rather than the only one.
evidence: capture.cpp:61 `uint32_t width = 0, height = 0, arraySize = 0, sampleCount = 0;`; :293 `info.arraySize = createInfo->arraySize;`; grep of arraySize in layer/src yields exactly two reads -- :298 (creation log, and that reads createInfo->arraySize, not the field) and :591 (status JSON). Dispatch sites :452 and :533 pass view.arrayIndex unvalidated; ResolveDepth passes view.depthArrayIndex the same way. Vulkan consumes it as subresourceRange.baseArrayLayer (capture_vulkan.cpp:594), VkImageResolve.srcSubresource (:621) and copyArrayLayer (:602) with no check -- and cannot self-check, since a VkImage handle carries no queryable layer count.
verify_note: CONFIRMED on the substantive claim; PARTIALLY REFUTED on the framing. Refuted: 'the only reader is a diagnostics dump' implies dead code -- the dump is really consumed (scripts/integration_hello_xr.mjs:157/225). Confirmed by grep that no validation reader exists, and by hooks_capture.cpp:107 (capture runs before the runtime's own xrEndFrame validation) that no downstream guard compensates. Same root gap as candidate 2 -- treat as one fix, not two; this is the superset (adds the Vulkan colour path and the depth path). Left unverified: whether any real app under test has ever submitted imageArrayIndex >= arraySize -- no repro exists in-repo, so this is a robustness/defence-in-depth gap, which is why severity is medium and not high.

what: The 'Defensive bounds check' at line 180-187 validates x/y/w/h against desc.Width/desc.Height but never validates arrayIndex against desc.ArraySize, even though `desc` is already populated two lines earlier (tex->GetDesc(&desc), line 161-162) and arrayIndex is fed straight into D3D11CalcSubresource(0, arrayIndex, desc.MipLevels) at line 261.
why_meaningless: Not meaningless, but incomplete relative to the contract its own comment states ('Better an honest error than a silently-broken image (CLAUDE.md)'). It validates one of the two app-supplied index inputs into the source texture and leaves the other unchecked, so the comment promises more coverage than the block delivers.
impact: An out-of-range arrayIndex reaches CopySubresourceRegion, which returns void -- no HRESULT to inspect. The freshly created staging texture keeps undefined contents and the function proceeds to Map/encode, returning {ok:true, path:...} with a black/garbage PNG: the exact silently-broken-image class the file's own comment (and the M0 flat-capture history in .claude/rules/native-win-interop.md) exists to prevent. Precondition is a spec-violating app, which is why this is medium and not high.
fix: Add `|| arrayIndex >= desc.ArraySize` to the existing guard at capture_d3d11.cpp:180 (or fix centrally in capture.cpp -- see candidate 3), mirroring capture_d3d12.cpp:159-162.
evidence: capture_d3d11.cpp:161-162 `D3D11_TEXTURE2D_DESC desc{}; tex->GetDesc(&desc);` (ArraySize available); :178-187 the guard, which tests only x/y/w/h; :261 `UINT srcSub = D3D11CalcSubresource(0, arrayIndex, desc.MipLevels);` used for the CopySubresourceRegion source. The D3D12 sibling DOES check: capture_d3d12.cpp:158-162 `const UINT arraySize = srcDesc.DepthOrArraySize ? ... : 1; if (arrayIndex >= arraySize) return fail("arrayIndex ... out of range ...");`.
verify_note: CONFIRMED. Tried and failed to refute via three routes. (a) 'The runtime validates imageArrayIndex before we ever touch the texture' -- FALSE: hooks_capture.cpp:103-110 shows Hook_xrEndFrame calls playspectra::CaptureOnEndFrame(frameEndInfo) at line 107 BEFORE `next(session, frameEndInfo)` at line 110, so the layer reads the texture before the runtime can reject the frame. (b) 'Something upstream clamps it' -- FALSE: grep of arrayIndex across layer/src shows capture.cpp:371 assigns pv.subImage.imageArrayIndex raw and passes it through at :452 (recording) and :533 (one-shot) with no check anywhere in between. (c) 'ArraySize isn't reachable here' -- FALSE, desc is in scope at line 178. The staging desc's `sdesc.ArraySize = 1` (line 194) is the destination, unrelated to the source guard.

what: DominantEyeIndex() の唯一の分岐である PLAYSPECTRA_DOMINANT_EYE=left 経路が、スイート全体でカバレッジゼロ。テストは env 未設定のデフォルト(戻り値 1)しか見ていない。
why_meaningless: capture_common.cpp:67-72 の関数本体は「env が "left" なら 0」の1分岐がすべてで、それ以外は定数 1 を返すだけ。DefaultIsRight および EyeToIndexTest の Dominant/Unknown 系(:118,:119)はいずれも env を設定しないため、`if (std::string(e) == "left") return 0;` の行は一度も実行されない。結果として、env 名の typo・比較文字列の変更・条件反転が入っても検知できず、関数の存在理由(利き目の切替可能性)は無検証のまま。逆向きの脆さもある: 開発者のシェルに PLAYSPECTRA_DOMINANT_EYE=left が残っていると、この3テストが『実装は正しいのに赤』になる(テストが ambient env に依存し hermetic でない)。
impact: eye 指定を省いた全スクリーンショット/録画が DominantEyeIndex の戻り値でどちらの目を書き出すか決めるため、この分岐は利き目切替という唯一の設定ノブそのもの。壊れてもユニット 82 テストは全緑のまま出荷され、env を設定した呼び出し元にだけ静かに効かなくなる。緩和材料として、README:169-174 の env 表に PLAYSPECTRA_DOMINANT_EYE は載っておらず(未文書)、実際に M0.5 の VR_AGENT_→PLAYSPECTRA_ 改名で変数名が変わっているのにそれを検知する装置も文書も無い。外部利用者の実害範囲は限定的なので high ではなく medium(『設定が効かないのに効くように見える』に該当)。
fix: env をセットして 0 を検証するケースを追加する。プロセス共有の gtest でのリークと実行順依存を避けるため RAII ガード(コンストラクタで旧値を保存 + _putenv_s/setenv、デストラクタで復元/削除)を用意し、(a) "left" → 0、(b) "right"/未知値 → 1、(c) ガード解除後にデフォルトへ戻ること、を検証する。同じガードを既存の DefaultIsRight にも被せて env を明示的に消せば、ambient env による偽 FAIL も同時に潰せる。
verify_note: 反証を2方向から試みたが成立せず。(1)「gtest はプロセス共有で env 変更が他テストへ漏れるため意図的に避けた設計では」→ 該当タスクの契約 .claude/harness/contracts/unit-tests-registry-capture.json の non_goals は InferHandTops(g_actions ランタイム依存)と AggregateFallback(内部状態依存)のみで、env 分岐の除外は一切書かれていない=意図的除外の一次証拠なし。しかも RAII ガードで解消可能な制約であり、除外の正当化にならない。(2)「DominantEyeIndex は実質デッドコードでは」→ 違う。control_channel.cpp:89/:280 で eye の既定値が "dominant"、capture.cpp:618 で録画既定も "dominant" なので、既定パスの全キャプチャがこの関数を通る(env 未設定時は定数 1 を返す固定路)。決定的根拠は grep の全数結果: PLAYSPECTRA_DOMINANT_EYE を設定するコード・スクリプト・CI がリポジトリ内に一つも存在せず、"left" 枝はテストバイナリ内で構造的に到達不能(到達する唯一の条件=ambient env がある場合は、逆に既存3テストが FAIL する)。

what: sRGB エンコードのべき乗枝(c>0.0031308)を実行する唯一のテストが EXPECT_GT/EXPECT_LT の広い区間チェック(0.5<v<1.0)だけで、係数・ガンマを一切拘束していない。
why_meaningless: LinearToSrgb(0.5) の正値は 1.055*0.5^(1/2.4)-0.055 = 0.7354 だが、テストは (0.5, 1.0) の区間しか見ない。1/2.4 を 1/2.2 に取り違えても 0.7148、1/2.0 でも 0.691 と区間内に収まり続けるため退行を検出できない。かつ端点テスト群はべき乗式を一切通らない: LinearToSrgb_One/_AboveOne/_PosInf は実装 pixel_convert.cpp:54 の `if (c >= 1.0f) return 1.0f;` の早期 return で返り、_Zero/_Negative/_NaN は :53 の早期 return、_LinearRegion は :55 の直線枝で返る。つまりべき乗枝(:56)を実行する唯一のテストが _MidRange であり、その唯一のテストが値を検証していない。knee 直上(0.0031309 付近)の区分連続性を見るテストも無い。
impact: LinearToSrgb は HDR(R16G16B16A16_FLOAT)キャプチャの色変換そのもので、3 API 全経路が通る: capture_d3d11.cpp:326 と capture_d3d12.cpp:372 が DecodeHdrRowsToSrgb 経由、capture_vulkan.cpp:690-692 が QuantizeSrgb 直呼び。ガンマ/係数の退行が入ってもユニット・E2E とも全緑のまま、HDR キャプチャ全フレームの中間輝度が静かにズレる(例: ガンマ 2.4→2.2 で 8bit 値 188→182)。ただし 8bit UNORM の通常経路は RepackRows でこの関数を通らないため、影響範囲は HDR swapchain のみ。
fix: EXPECT_NEAR(LinearToSrgb(0.5f), 1.055f*std::pow(0.5f,1.0f/2.4f)-0.055f, 1e-5f)(または既知値 0.735357f をハードコードし導出をコメント)に置き換え、直線枝テスト(:81-84)と対称の厳密性にする。加えて (a) knee 直上 0.0031309f で 12.92*0.0031308 との連続性、(b) もう1点(0.2 か 0.8)を追加すると、指数・両係数の3自由度が一意に固定される。
evidence:
layer/src/pixel_convert.cpp:52-57
  if (!(c > 0.0f)) return 0.0f;   // _Zero/_Negative/_NaN はここで返る
  if (c >= 1.0f) return 1.0f;     // _One/_AboveOne/_PosInf はここで返る(式を通らない)
  if (c <= 0.0031308f) return c * 12.92f;  // _LinearRegion はここ
  return 1.055f * std::pow(c, 1.0f / 2.4f) - 0.055f;  // ← 検証するテストは :86 の区間チェックのみ

リポジトリ全体 grep (build/_deps・third_party・runtime 除く) で 1.055 / 12.92 / 2.4f の出現は layer/src/pixel_convert.cpp:55-56 と layer/tests/test_pixel_convert.cpp:83(直線枝の EXPECT_NEAR)のみ。厳密な中間値検証は他に一件も無い。
QuantizeSrgb のテスト(test_pixel_convert.cpp:94-104)も 0.0/1.0/-1.0 の端点のみ。
DecodeHdrRowsToSrgb のテスト(test_capture_common.cpp:89-114)は自コメント :87 で「値は sRGB 変換の丸めに依存しない端点(0.0->0, 1.0->255)のみを使う」と明言。
E2E も色を固定していない: scripts/integration_hello_xr.mjs:253-265 の HDR ゲートは shot.tonemapped / colorConversion / sourceHdrFormat のメタデータのみ検査、ピクセル側は :232 の distinctColors>=3 && dominantFraction<0.999(退化検査)のみ。tools/playspectra_png_stats.py も色数・優勢色率の統計のみ。golden 画像/期待色照合は repo に無い(grep golden/sha256 → scripts/e2e_playwright_loop.sh:78 のフレーム間差分ハッシュのみ)。
verify_note: 反証を3方向から試みたが、いずれも成立せず。(1)「別の箇所で厳密に検証されている」→ 上記の全リポジトリ grep とテスト読解で、中間輝度の sRGB 係数を固定する検証は repo 内に一件も存在しない(test_capture_common.cpp:87 のコメントが端点限定であることを自ら明言、E2E は tonemapped フラグと退化検査のみ)。(2)「pow の実装差でプラットフォーム依存になるので意図的に緩めた」→ 同ファイル :83 の姉妹テストが EXPECT_NEAR 1e-6 を使っている前例があり、1e-5 なら libm 差は十分吸収する。契約 .claude/harness/contracts/r11-unit-tests.json の dod は「covers LinearToSrgb」のみで緩さを意図した記述も non_goal も無い。(3)「端点テストが係数を縛る」→ 縛らない。上記のとおり全端点が早期 return で処理され、べき乗式は _MidRange 以外どのテストからも一度も評価されない(これが決定的根拠)。severity は提案の high から medium に引き下げ: 現行の係数は標準 sRGB EOTF^-1 と一致しており今は正しく、影響も HDR 16F 経路限定なので「今壊れている」ではなく「壊れても緑(退行検知不能)」に該当する。

what: null compositor が frame_interval_ns を 20FPS 固定にし、引数で受け取っている xdev の申告値(PlaySpectra HMD: 1/90秒)を参照しない。この値は (1) u_pc_fake のペーシング周期、(2) sys_info->refresh_rates_hz[0](= xrGetDisplayRefreshRate の応答)の両方を決める。
why_meaningless: 申告値を読む配線が同じ関数の引数として既に来ており(xdev は view_count・blend modes・解像度に使われている)、本流 main compositor は同じ値を comp_settings.c:99 `uint64_t interval_ns = xdev->hmd->screens[0].nominal_frame_interval_ns;` で読む設計。null compositor だけがテストスタブ定数のまま。結果として PlaySpectra 自身の申告が内部で二重化・矛盾する: 制御チャネルの descriptor は refresh_hz:90 を返す(control.c:311)のに、同じスタックの OpenXR ランタイムはアプリへ 20Hz を返す。
impact: headless(XRT_COMPOSITOR_NULL=1 — scripts/lib_monado_stack.sh:43, run_hello_xr_monado.sh, e2e_playwright_loop.sh すべてこの経路)での観測レートが HMD の申告に関係なく 20fps に張り付く。北極星の「画面を観察する」ループのスループット上限が実デバイス想定(90Hz)の 1/4.5 で、Server の注入は 60Hz(playspectra_server.py:218 rate_hz=60.0)なので注入と観測のレートも噛み合わない。加えて xrGetDisplayRefreshRateFB が 20 を返し、driver descriptor の refresh_hz:90 と矛盾する。ただし現状これで壊れて緑になっているテストは無い(refresh_rate を検証するテストは repo 内0件・grep で確認)ので high ではなく、『退行を検知できない・申告値が効かないのに効くように見える』の medium。
fix: 解像度バグの修正パッチと同型に揃える: `int64_t iv = xdev->hmd->screens[0].nominal_frame_interval_ns; c->settings.frame_interval_ns = iv > 0 ? iv : U_TIME_1S_IN_NS / 20;`(xdev 優先・0のときだけ従来定数へフォールバック)。値の出所を1本化するため、control.c:311 の descriptor refresh_hz も同じ xdev 値から算出するのが望ましい。併せて「headless の申告 refresh が HMD 宣言に一致する」ことを機械判定する項目を tools 側に1件足す(現状 0件で退行検知が無い)。
evidence: null_compositor.c:642 `c->settings.frame_interval_ns = U_TIME_1S_IN_NS / 20; // 20 FPS` の直後 :643 `c->xdev = xdev;`。消費先: :260 `u_pc_fake_create(c->settings.frame_interval_ns, ...)`、:365 `sys_info->refresh_rates_hz[0] = (float)(1. / time_ns_to_s(c->settings.frame_interval_ns));`、:590 `*out_display_refresh_rate_hz = c->sys_info.refresh_rates_hz[0];`。申告側: playspectra_hmd.c:163 `hmd->base.hmd->screens[0].nominal_frame_interval_ns = time_s_to_ns(1.0f / 90.0f);`。ペーシング伝播も追跡済み: comp_multi_system.c:553 が null の predict_frame を呼び、:571 broadcast_timings_to_pacers → :410 `u_pa_info(mc->upa, ..., predicted_display_period_ns, ...)`、その period は u_pacing_compositor_fake.c pc_predict の `ft->frame_period_ns`(= 生成時の frame_interval)。つまりアプリの xrWaitFrame 周期が 50ms に固定される。
verify_note: 事実関係は全て一次ソースで確認、反証は成立せず。ただし候補の記述に対する重要な補正が2点。(1) **この20FPS定数は PlaySpectra が書いたものではなく upstream Monado の原文**: `git diff HEAD -- src/xrt/compositor/null/null_compositor.c` の差分は解像度修正(compositor_init_sys_info の 29 行)のみで frame_interval 行は無改変、`git log -L 642,642` は初出コミット c976c5400 「c/null: Add null compositor」= 追加時からのスタブ定数(320x240 と同じ素性)。よって『同じファイルに残った同一パターン』という候補の構図は正しいが、これは本 repo が持ち込んだ退行ではなく vendored upstream のスタブを引き継いでいる状態。(2) **『黙って壊れる』は言い過ぎ**: 実測は 20FPS 前提のまま hello_xr×capture 20/20・capture 60/60 が通っており、壊れているのは正しさではなくスループットと申告値の一貫性。それでも CONFIRMED としたのは、(a) xdev が引数で渡っているのに読まないという指摘自体が客観的に真、(b) 値が pacing と refresh 応答という実挙動2箇所に効く、(c) 本 repo は同じ関数の解像度スタブを『null compositor は CI 用途=PlaySpectra の用途そのもの。スタブ定数のまま残っていただけ』という理由で既に修正しており、同じ論拠がそのまま当てはまるため。

what: set_state で left/right に "connected":false を明示送信しても apply_ctrl が即 return し、共有 state の connected は書き換わらない。にもかかわらず応答は ok:true / applied:true。結果、st.connected を false にする経路がドライバ内に一つも存在しない。
why_meaningless: 下流の「非接続時の振る舞い」は両側とも完全に実装済みなのに、それを駆動する入力側が無いため到達不能: (a) 出力側 control.c:268-271 は st.connected==false のとき `{"connected":false}` だけを返す分岐を持つ、(b) device 側 playspectra_controller.c:96-99 は in->active=st.connected + 値ゼロクリアという OpenXR 可視の正しい切断表現を持つ。両方とも実行され得ない。加えて spec §2.2 は「hmd/left/right の3キーは常に present(未接続は {"connected":false})」と規定しており、準拠クライアントはキー省略をしないので、現実装の「省略 == connected:false == 何もしない」という縮退は、キー省略の互換のためですらない。
impact: 「コントローラを外した/電源が切れた」をVR版Playwrightのシナリオとして注入できない。クライアントは applied:true を受け取るのに state は不変で、直後の get_state は connected:true と古い grip/aim を返し続ける=「設定が効かないのに効いたように見える」偽成功。OpenXR アプリからは常に isActive=true にしか見えず、接続喪失時のアプリ挙動(アクション非活性・プロファイル喪失)を検証できない。既存テストを緑のまま壊す性質ではない(切断を試すテストが1件も無い)ため high ではないが、注入面の1次元が無言で no-op になる点で medium。

what: After downloading the Monado Windows CI artifact zip, an inline python heredoc extracts every entry under 'install/' (minus the SteamVR driver share) into third_party/monado/, counts the files into `n`, and prints 'extracted {n} files'. The script then unconditionally writes VERSION.txt and prints its success messages.
why_meaningless: `n` is never checked and the script never verifies the file its own final line advertises (`${DEST}/openxr_monado.json`). If the CI artifact layout changes (output no longer nested under 'install/') or no path matches, n=0, nothing is written, and the script prints exactly the same 'done. runtime json: ...' as a complete, correct fetch.
impact: A zero-file extraction is indistinguishable from success in this script's output. Because there is no downstream backstop either — integration_test.sh:26 and integration_openvr_test.sh:15 set XR_RUNTIME_JSON to third_party/monado/openxr_monado.json without checking it exists — a stale or missing Monado tree is never caught: a broken re-fetch leaves the previous build in place while claiming the requested `$REF` was fetched, and every VR_RUNTIME=monado run then silently exercises an old build (or, if the tree is absent entirely, whatever the OpenXR loader falls back to; integration_test.sh:21's own comment records that an unusable XR_RUNTIME_JSON 'would fall back to SteamVR').
fix: Fail loudly on an empty extraction (`if n == 0: sys.exit('no install/ entries in artifact -- layout changed?')`) and assert `[ -f "$DEST/openxr_monado.json" ]` in the shell before writing VERSION.txt and printing the success lines.
evidence: setup_monado.sh:20-29 `n = 0` / `for i in z.infolist(): if i.filename.startswith('install/') ... n += 1` / `print(f'extracted {n} files -> {dest}')`; 32 `echo "[setup_monado] ref=... fetched ..." > "${DEST}/VERSION.txt"`; 33 `echo "[setup_monado] done. runtime json: ${DEST}/openxr_monado.json"`. No `sys.exit` on n==0, no `[ -f "$DEST/openxr_monado.json" ]` assertion anywhere in the file.
verify_note: Confirmed by direct code reading: `n` has exactly one consumer (the print at line 29) and there is no existence check on the promised runtime json. This is also the exact backstop the repo's own rule demands — .claude/rules/setup-scripts.md #1 ('ダウンロード物には機械検査のバックストップを必ず置く', exemplified by setup_opencomposite.sh's PE-header check) — and the -fSL half of that follow-up was applied to this file in 1b9aa0eda while the post-extract assertion was not. Two nuances that refine (but do not refute) the finding. (a) `set -eu` plus `curl -fSL` do cover the adjacent failure modes: an HTTP error aborts at line 13, and a non-zip/corrupt payload raises BadZipFile which aborts the script. The uncovered case is precisely 'valid zip, zero matching entries'. (b) In that case the script accidentally fails on a FRESH machine: `${DEST}` is never mkdir'd by the shell (only inside the python loop, per matched entry), so with n==0 and no pre-existing third_party/monado the `> "${DEST}/VERSION.txt"` redirect at line 32 dies under set -e. I confirmed third_party/ currently holds only README.md ('Nothing here is committed'), so today the failure would be loud. The silent-success path is therefore specifically the re-fetch-over-an-existing-tree case — which is exactly the 'stale build masked as fresh' scenario the finding describes, so the finding stands.

what: In the FOCUSED branch (lines 175-223) the return values of xrSyncActions, xrGetActionStateVector2f, xrGetActionStateFloat and xrLocateSpace are all discarded (not even assigned), and tsv.isActive / trv.isActive / loc.locationFlags are only fed to printf. `reads++` (line 204) is unconditional, and the process exit code is `reads > 0 ? 0 : 2` (line 234).
why_meaningless: `reads` is a counter of 'the FOCUSED loop body executed', not of 'a controller input was actually synced/active'. Every OpenXR call in that block can fail (or return isActive=0 because the /interaction_profiles/oculus/touch_controller binding never resolved) for the entire run and the process still exits 0. The exit code therefore cannot distinguish 'injection reached the action system' from 'the action system delivered nothing at all'.
impact: This is the only place in the repo where injected controller input is observed from the OpenXR *application* side. The downstream suites that use this probe as their host (tools/playspectra_frame_test.py, playspectra_reset_test.py, playspectra_multiobs_test.py) all assert through the control channel :52702 (adapter side) and never look at the app's action state, so a regression in interaction-profile binding or xrSyncActions is invisible to every automated test. `.claude/playspectra-m2-status.md:193` cites this probe as the sole evidence for '入力E2E検証済み'. Not rated high because no script consumes this probe's rc (verified: grep for the probe/binary names across scripts/, run_all_tests.sh and the test suites returns only doc + self-comment hits), and the per-frame printf does expose active=%d to a human reader — so the failure mode today is 'documented as verified with no regression gate', not 'a CI gate goes green'. It becomes high the moment anyone wires `ps_action_probe || fail=1` into a script.
fix: Track a separate counter, e.g. `if (xrSyncActions(...) == XR_SUCCESS && tsv.isActive && trv.isActive) active_reads++;`, keep `reads` for loop bookkeeping/haptic scheduling, and return non-zero with a distinct message when the loop completed in FOCUSED but active_reads == 0 (and likewise when any of the four calls returned != XR_SUCCESS). That preserves the current 'never reached FOCUSED -> 2' signal while making 'reached FOCUSED but no input ever arrived' fail loudly.
evidence: tools/playspectra_action_probe.c:180 `xrSyncActions(sess, &syncInfo);` (rc dropped) / :186 `xrGetActionStateVector2f(sess, &gi, &tsv);` (rc dropped) / :189 `xrGetActionStateFloat(sess, &gi, &trv);` (rc dropped) / :196 `xrLocateSpace(gripSpace, stage, t, &loc);` (rc dropped) / :198-202 isActive and locationFlags appear only inside printf / :204 `reads++;` unconditional / :234 `return reads > 0 ? 0 : 2;`. Contrast the same file's own CHK() macro (:19-27), which does hard-fail on XrResult for every setup call — the discipline is dropped exactly at the measurement.
verify_note: Read the whole file. Tried to reject three ways, all failed: (a) 'the printed values are the real assertion' — true, and the m2-status doc does quote measured before/after values, but that only means rc was never the evidence, it does not make rc correct; the tool still emits '[act] done, N focused reads' + rc=0 as a success signal. (b) 'a stricter check exists elsewhere' — searched: frame/reset/multiobs tests assert only via :52702 (adapter state), integration_hello_xr.mjs observes the layer, playspectra_coupling_probe.py asserts head pose only; nothing asserts app-side action state. (c) 'rc is intentionally just a host-liveness signal' — plausible as intent, but it is undocumented and directly conflicts with .claude/rules/review-checklist.md lens 5 ('実アプリ結合の完了判定は機械値で行う。プロセス生存・初期化ログ1行は根拠にしない'), which this rc is an instance of. Code facts are decisive; only the blast radius is bounded, hence medium not high.

symbol: check("walk_forward returns state (no error)") / strafe / press
what: The three checks at lines 86-91 assert only `isinstance(r, str) and len(r) > 0` on the tool's return text. The corresponding MCP tools unconditionally `return json.dumps(_state())` (tools/playspectra_mcp.py:72, 80, 87), which is always a long non-empty JSON string regardless of what the wrapper did.
why_meaningless: The assertion is satisfied by the tool's return-type contract alone, so it can never fail for a behavioural reason. Deleting the body of the wrapper (`srv().walk_forward(speed, duration_ms, hand)`) and leaving only the `return json.dumps(_state())` keeps all three checks green. Worse, it does not even meet its own stated goal of '(no error)': per MCP semantics a tool that raises is returned as a CallToolResult with isError=True carrying TextContent with the error message — `_text()` returns that message, which is a non-empty str, so the check still PASSES. The neighbouring checks are accidentally protected by `json.loads(_text(...))` (lines 41/45/49/66/72/77/93), which would raise on error text; these three are the only ones that skip json.loads, i.e. exactly the ones with no real assertion.
impact: Locomotion is a primary injection path for the project's 'VR版Playwright' north star, and this is the only coverage of the MCP-wrapper layer for walk_forward/strafe/press. A no-op or mis-mapped agent-facing wrapper ships with playspectra_mcp_verify.py fully green. Not high because (a) the script is a manual live-stack E2E, not part of scripts/run_all_tests.sh, and (b) the underlying Server methods do have real (if partial) assertions elsewhere — see verify_note.
fix: Assert an observable effect rather than a return type. Two workable signals, both available today: (1) `_state()` includes a monotonic `sequence` (playspectra_server.py:189-190 emits it; the adapter returns it in get_state — runtime/monado-playspectra/src/xrt/drivers/playspectra/playspectra_control.c:528), so read sequence before/after and assert it advanced by roughly rate_hz * duration_ms/1000 frames — a no-op wrapper advances it by 0. (2) Assert the released-to-neutral post-state on the *specific* axis and hand actually requested (`left.inputs['/input/thumbstick/y']` for walk_forward, `/input/thumbstick/x` for strafe, `right` `/button/a/click` is False for press) so a hand/axis mis-mapping fails. Best is both, plus wrapping in `json.loads()` so an isError text response raises instead of passing.
evidence: tools/playspectra_mcp_verify.py:86-91 `rw = _text(await session.call_tool("walk_forward", ...)); check("walk_forward returns state (no error)", isinstance(rw, str) and len(rw) > 0, ...)` (same shape for strafe and press). tools/playspectra_mcp.py:69-87 — all three wrappers end in `return json.dumps(_state())`. The block's own comment (playspectra_mcp_verify.py:63-64) states the intent: 'exercise the remaining tools so an arg-mapping bug in the agent-facing wrapper (like the scenario `trigger` vs `set_trigger` name mismatch found this session) can't hide' — an arg-mapping bug (e.g. speed/duration_ms swapped, or hand ignored) produces a non-empty JSON string and hides anyway.
verify_note: The candidate's supporting premise is FACTUALLY WRONG and I am rejecting that part: 'this is the only place these two locomotion entry points are exercised at all in the test suite' is false. tools/playspectra_server.py:555-558 (verify_run, i.e. `--verify`) calls `srv.walk_forward(1.0, 200)` and asserts `abs(ty) < 1e-3` on left `/input/thumbstick/y`, and tools/scenarios/operate_completeness.json:15-16 runs `strafe` and asserts `/input/thumbstick/x` near 0. However, both of those assert only the RELEASE, which a no-op also satisfies (Server.walk_forward at playspectra_server.py:274-280 sets the axis during _stream then writes 0.0 and re-emits — the held value is unobservable from a post-hoc get_state), so the hold itself is unasserted everywhere in the repo, and the MCP wrapper layer specifically has no effect assertion at all. Core finding therefore CONFIRMED, premise corrected. The isError-passes-the-check point relies on MCP protocol/SDK semantics (tool errors returned in-band with isError:true rather than raised); I could not verify it empirically here because `mcp` is not installed in this environment (`import mcp` resolves to the repo's own legacy mcp/ directory as a namespace package — the known false-positive noted in the python-deps-use-venv memory). The main finding does not depend on that point.

what: The check requires an exact match `shot.height === sc.height` only when sc.height is truthy; when cap.swapchains is empty/missing it silently degrades to `shot.height > 100`.

what: colortype から算出した ch を stride/defilter には使うのに、色サンプル抽出だけ ch を無視して常に3バイト固定で読む (`key = bytes(line[x*ch : x*ch+3])`)。
why_meaningless: ch<3 (colortype 0/3/4 = grayscale・palette・grayscale+alpha) では『1ピクセルの色』ではなく隣接ピクセルを跨いだバイト列を色として数えることになり、distinctColors/dominantFraction が実ピクセル値と対応しない。
impact: 現行 repo からは到達不能。PNG 生成元は2つだけで、(a) layer/src/capture_common.cpp:49 `lodepng::encode(path, pixels, w, h, LCT_RGBA, 8)` = ct 6 / ch 4 → スライス正しい、(b) layer/src/capture_vulkan.cpp:887 `lodepng::encode(path, png, w, h, LCT_GREY, 16)` (深度マップ) = ct 0 だが **16bit** で、50行の `if bd != 8 ... return info` により画素ループ前に弾かれる。さらに flat-fill 検知の向きは grayscale でも保たれる (単色 → 全 key 同一 → distinct=1, dominant=1.0 で正しく degenerate)。具体的な偽PASS は『8bit・階調2種類だけの gray/palette PNG』(真の distinct=2 が最大8トリプルに膨らみ min_colors=3 を超える) という狭いケース。

what: `XrResult lr = xrLocateSpace(view, stage, t, &loc);` is captured only to be printed as `lr=%d`, never compared to XR_SUCCESS, and `loc.locationFlags` is likewise only printed. `printed++` is gated solely on the timespec->XrTime conversion (`toTime(...) == XR_SUCCESS && t != 0`), and the exit code is `printed > 0 ? 0 : 2`.
why_meaningless: The exit code answers 'did the session begin and did the clock conversion work at least once', not 'did the runtime return a valid tracked head pose'. A runtime that fails xrLocateSpace every iteration, or returns locationFlags=0x0 with a zeroed pose, still yields rc=0.
impact: Lower than candidate 1 because the property this probe checks by eye — runtime-level head-pose injection actually reaching an OpenXR consumer — IS machine-asserted elsewhere and IS gated in a script: tools/playspectra_coupling_probe.py asserts `abs(dz - expected_dz) < 0.3` AND `dx,dy < 0.3` (no sideways drift) and returns non-zero otherwise, and scripts/run_hello_xr_monado.sh:52-56 folds its rc into the run verdict (`RC=$(( IRC != 0 ? IRC : CRC ))`). So the weak rc here is a redundant manual diagnostic, not the load-bearing gate. Residual harm: .claude/playspectra-m2-status.md:29/45 presents this probe as the M2.2/M2.3 pose verification, so a reader may treat its rc=0 as verification.
fix: Gate the counter on the actual read: `if (lr == XR_SUCCESS && (loc.locationFlags & XR_SPACE_LOCATION_POSITION_VALID_BIT)) printed++;` (optionally counting failed/untracked samples separately and printing both), so 'session ran but every locate was invalid' exits non-zero instead of 0.
evidence: tools/playspectra_headless_probe.c:93 `if (toTime(inst, &ts, &t) == XR_SUCCESS && t != 0) {` — the only gate; :95 `XrResult lr = xrLocateSpace(view, stage, t, &loc);` with lr used only at :100 inside printf; :102 `printed++;` unconditional inside that block; :115 `return printed > 0 ? 0 : 2;`. Same CHK()-vs-measurement inconsistency as the action probe (:20-28 hard-fails setup calls).
verify_note: Read the whole file plus playspectra_coupling_probe.py and scripts/run_hello_xr_monado.sh. Attempted rejection 'the same property is asserted strictly elsewhere' — this SUCCEEDS as a severity argument (coupling_probe.py does precise z-tracking + no-drift assertions and its rc gates the script) but does NOT rescue this file: the code fact stands that rc is independent of xrLocateSpace's result. Also note the gate is stronger than the candidate implies — rc=0 additionally requires instance/system/session/space creation (all CHK-guarded) plus a READY event and a successful xrBeginSession — so it is not 'green on a totally dead stack', only 'green on a stack whose pose reads are broken'. Downgraded to low accordingly.

what: hellovr_dx12.exe and monado-service.exe are force-killed, the script sleeps 1s, starts a NEW monado-service, sleeps 3s, starts NEW hellovr_dx12, then polls netstat for '127.0.0.1:52700 .*LISTENING' up to 30 times to decide the control channel is ready.
why_meaningless: Same class as integration_test.sh:41 and explicitly documented/fixed in lib_monado_stack.sh:57-58: no wait for the OLD process's 52700 listener to actually disappear before the NEW app is started and the same port is immediately polled, so the poll can latch onto the dying process and short-circuit its own 30s budget.
impact: A false ok=1 leaves only the fixed `sleep 5` at line 43 before `node "$CLIENT" 52700`; if OpenComposite's session has not reached FOCUSED by then the client fails and the sole OpenVR-path integration test reports a spurious FAIL on a correct build.
fix: Same as integration_test.sh: wait for 52700 to actually clear (reuse lib_monado_stack.sh's loop) before launching the new app, and add a real readiness check for monado-service instead of the flat `sleep 3`.
evidence: integration_openvr_test.sh:26-38 `taskkill //F //IM hellovr_dx12.exe //IM monado-service.exe`; 27 `sleep 1`; 28 monado-service start; 29 `sleep 3`; 32 `( cd "$APP_DIR" && ./hellovr_dx12.exe ... ) &`; 35-38 `for i in $(seq 1 30); do if netstat -ano | grep -q "127.0.0.1:52700 .*LISTENING"; then ok=1; break; fi; sleep 1; done`.
verify_note: Same verdict and reasoning as candidate 3, and the same narrowing counter-evidence applies: the graceful gate at lines 55-67 waits for 'control_channel: accept loop exited' before the force-kill at line 70, so on the green path 52700 is already free when the script exits; SO_REUSEADDR (layer/src/control_channel.cpp:379-381) means a lingering old listener does not block the new bind, only the poll's discrimination; LISTENING cannot be a TIME_WAIT remnant. Not reproduced, hence PLAUSIBLE. Two observations the candidate did not make, both stronger than the stated race in this file: (1) the new monado-service gets no readiness check at all — a flat `sleep 3` (line 29) and no port/pipe probe, so a service that failed to start (e.g. the old one still owning the named pipe after the 1s sleep) surfaces only as ok=0 -> rc=1, i.e. as a spurious red with a misleading 'control channel never came up' message; (2) the hellovr launch at line 32 is a subshell with no PID captured, so unlike integration_test.sh there is no liveness fallback at all if the app dies during the 30s poll.

what: hello_xr.exe is force-killed, the script sleeps a flat 1s (plus 1s+3s more for VR_RUNTIME=monado), starts a NEW hello_xr, then polls `netstat -ano | grep '127.0.0.1:52700 .*LISTENING'` up to 30 times to decide the new control channel is up.
why_meaningless: The readiness poll cannot distinguish the NEW layer's listener from the OLD (dying) process's still-open listening socket, so a false ok=1 short-circuits the 30s readiness budget. The repo's own scripts/lib_monado_stack.sh:57-62 documents this exact hazard ('taskkill //F is async: wait for a prior run's ports to actually free before we bind, else the readiness check latches onto the DYING process (this flaked back-to-back \'all\' runs)') and fixes it with a wait-for-port-free loop that integration_test.sh lacks.
impact: On a re-run shortly after a hello_xr was force-killed (the contracts in .claude/harness/contracts/m0-d3d11-flat-capture.json prescribe four integration_test.sh runs back to back), a false ok=1 skips the 30s wait and leaves only the fixed `sleep 6` at line 70 before `node "$CLIENT" 52700`. If the new session has not reached FOCUSED by then the client hits connection-refused and the run reports a spurious FAIL on GAP-10, the primary engine-independence test.
fix: Reuse (or port) lib_monado_stack.sh's wait-for-port-free loop before line 57 so the poll can only ever observe the NEW process's socket.
evidence: integration_test.sh:41 `taskkill //F //IM hello_xr.exe ...`; 51 `sleep 1`; 57 `( sleep 85 & ... ) | "$HELLO" -g "$GFX" ... &`; 62-65 `for i in $(seq 1 30); do if netstat -ano | grep -q "127.0.0.1:52700 .*LISTENING"; then ok=1; ... done`. Contrast lib_monado_stack.sh:56-63 `taskkill //F //IM monado-service.exe` + `for i in $(seq 1 20); do if ! mstack_listen 52702 && ! mstack_listen 52700; then break; fi; sleep 0.5; done`.
verify_note: The structural gap is confirmed by code: the documented-and-fixed pattern exists at lib_monado_stack.sh:57-62 and has no counterpart here — only `sleep 1`. Kept at PLAUSIBLE because three pieces of counter-evidence narrow the window substantially and I could not reproduce it. (a) On the green path the PREVIOUS run's graceful gate (integration_test.sh:102-115) blocks until the layer logs 'control_channel: accept loop exited', i.e. 52700 is already released before that run exits — the stale-listener window only exists after a prior run that failed or was aborted before the graceful gate. (b) I checked the mechanism the finding implies for the new process and it does NOT apply: layer/src/control_channel.cpp:379-381 sets SO_REUSEADDR before bind (line 388), and on Windows SO_REUSEADDR permits binding a port another socket already holds, so the new layer's bind does not fail on a lingering old listener — the damage is confined to the readiness poll being short-circuited, not to the new channel being unable to come up. (c) A listening socket never enters TIME_WAIT, so `LISTENING` can only match a process still alive; the residual risk is exactly 'GPU app lingering >1s under TerminateProcess', which is credible for D3D/Vulkan apps but unmeasured. No journal entry records this flake for integration_test.sh specifically; the documented flake was lib_monado_stack's monado-service on 52702.

what: HalfFloatSelfTest() runs once on the first HDR frame decode and its bool result is discarded with `(void)kHalfTested;`. A FAIL produces one line in the layer log file and nothing else -- the HDR decode continues, the PNG is written, the request returns ok:true.
why_meaningless: As a *gate* it is inert: nothing consumes the result and no script parses the log for 'HalfFloatSelfTest: FAIL' (grepped repo-wide, excluding build/: only capture_vulkan.cpp itself, test_pixel_convert.cpp:9's comment, and .claude/harness notes match). But it is not meaningless as a *diagnostic*, and the candidate's stated impact does not survive contact with the repo.
impact: Limited to a misleading impression that the shipped HDR path is runtime-guarded. The regression it nominally guards is already gated: layer/tests/test_pixel_convert.cpp:9 says verbatim '// --- HalfToFloat (cases from capture_vulkan.cpp HalfFloatSelfTest + extras) ---' and provides 10 gtests (Zero/NegativeZero/One/Half/NegativeOne/MaxNormal/SmallestSubnormal/Inf/NegInf/NaN) over the SAME pixel_convert.cpp:16 HalfToFloat the layer calls; scripts/run_all_tests.sh:50-53 builds playspectra_test and runs ctest with rc propagation. A bit-shuffle regression therefore turns the local test gate red -- it is NOT invisible.
fix: Leave as-is, or (if churn is acceptable) delete the runtime self-test and keep the gtest coverage. Do NOT adopt the 'return {ok:false, error:"HDR decode self-test failed"}' half of the proposed fix without deciding it deliberately: the layer runs inside third-party apps where ctest cannot run, and a shipped-binary/toolchain-specific float regression (MinGW layer DLL vs MSVC test exe, fast-math flags) is exactly what an in-binary self-test can catch and the separately-compiled gtest cannot.
evidence: capture_vulkan.cpp:683-684 `static const bool kHalfTested = HalfFloatSelfTest(); (void)kHalfTested;`; capture_vulkan.cpp:438 `Log(std::string("HalfFloatSelfTest: ") + (ok ? "pass" : "FAIL"));`; capture_vulkan.cpp:46 `void Log(...) { LayerLog("capture", ...); }`; layer_log.cpp:45-55 LayerLog writes ONLY to the $PLAYSPECTRA_LOG / %TEMP% file (no stderr, no exit code).
verify_note: REFUTED two of the candidate's load-bearing claims. (1) 'a real regression here is invisible outside a human manually reading the log' -- false: test_pixel_convert.cpp carries the identical case set and is wired into the local gate (scripts/run_all_tests.sh:53 `ctest --test-dir layer/build -E loader_test --output-on-failure || fail`), and layer/build/playspectra_test[1]_tests.cmake confirms the 10 PixelConvertTest.HalfToFloat_* tests are registered. (2) 'defeating the never-a-silently-broken-image requirement' -- overstated for the same reason. CONFIRMED the mechanical facts: result discarded, log-file-only sink, no log-scraping consumer. Also found the retention is a *recorded deliberate decision*, not drift: .claude/harness/contracts/r03-pixel-convert.json lists 'HalfFloatSelfTest (Log-dependent) remain in capture_vulkan.cpp' as in-scope-to-keep and explicitly scopes out 'turning HalfFloatSelfTest into a real unit test (that is R11)'; backlog.md:117 records R11 shipped (45d2d2f) as 'プロダクションコード変更なし'. Not REJECTED only because the comment's word 'loudly' does oversell a file-log line. Left unverified: whether the layer DLL and playspectra_test are ever built with divergent float flags (which would be the self-test's remaining justification).

what: The GAP-08 non-CA override substitutes the single global emulated profile for ANY topLevelUserPath: the parameter is forwarded to the runtime but never consulted by the override, whose condition looks only at the runtime's XrResult and at profileState->interactionProfile == XR_NULL_PATH.
why_meaningless: Mechanically true and uncompensated anywhere else — but the harm is conditional on an app behaviour that no code in this repository exhibits, so it is a latent fidelity gap rather than an observed defect. It is also not documented as a deliberate simplification (unlike FallbackNoteSuggestedProfile's 'FIRST profile only'), so a reader cannot tell intent from oversight.
impact: In non-CA fallback mode only (PLAYSPECTRA_DISABLE_CA / a runtime without XR_EXT_conformance_automation): an app querying a top-level path the emulated device does not represent (/user/head, /user/gamepad, /user/treadmill) is told the controller interaction profile is current there. Same line also rewrites ANY runtime failure — including XR_ERROR_PATH_UNSUPPORTED for a genuinely unsupported path, XR_ERROR_HANDLE_INVALID, XR_ERROR_SESSION_LOST — into XR_SUCCESS plus a fabricated profile, which the candidate did not name and which is the sharper half of the same root cause. Capture and injection themselves are unaffected; no test turns green or red because of this.
fix: Record the top-level path(s) covered by the suggested bindings (available in Hook_xrSuggestInteractionProfileBindings via each XrActionSuggestedBinding's binding path prefix) and have the fallback lookup take topLevelUserPath, firing only for covered paths. Separately, narrow the trigger: override on 'runtime succeeded but reported XR_NULL_PATH' and, if failure-override is still wanted, restrict it to the specific error the target runtime returns for 'no device' rather than blanket XR_FAILED(r), so session-loss/handle errors keep propagating. If instead the path-agnostic behaviour is intended, say so in the comment at :153-154 the way input_inject.h:75 documents 'FIRST profile only'.
evidence: layer/src/hooks_action.cpp:164-168 — `if (emulated != XR_NULL_PATH && (XR_FAILED(r) || profileState->interactionProfile == XR_NULL_PATH)) { profileState->interactionProfile = emulated; r = XR_SUCCESS; }` — topLevelUserPath appears only in the pass-through call at :160. layer/src/input_inject.cpp:230 — `XrPath FallbackCurrentProfile() { return g_emulated_profile; }` takes no path argument; g_emulated_profile is set once from the FIRST suggested profile (input_inject.cpp:245-248). grep for 'CurrentInteractionProfile' across layer/src returns only this hook, its header, the dispatch slot and the accessor — no path filter exists anywhere. Commit 160cdbdd9 (GAP-08) states the intent as '非CAアプリが仮想コントローラーを認識' with no per-path scoping; .claude/refactor-plan.md mentions GAP-08 only structurally.
verify_note: The mechanism is confirmed by code (no path check exists anywhere in layer/src; FallbackCurrentProfile has no path parameter), so this is not a fact error. What I could NOT establish, and why it stays PLAUSIBLE rather than CONFIRMED: (1) no in-repo app reaches the branch with a non-hand path — hello_xr, the only app driven by the automated suites including the NO_CA fallback run, never calls xrGetCurrentInteractionProfile at all (grep of layer/build/_deps/openxr_sdk-src/src/tests/hello_xr/*.cpp: 0 hits), and scripts/integration_*.mjs never issue such a query either; (2) whether the real targets (Godot VRDevApp, Unity/Unreal apps) query /user/head or /user/gamepad is learned knowledge, not a repo-backed fact — per CLAUDE.md I must label that a hypothesis, and its verification method is to run VRDevApp under PLAYSPECTRA_DISABLE_CA=1 with an xrGetCurrentInteractionProfile trace; (3) the layer's own intended job ('let the non-CA app see the virtual controller') IS accomplished, so this is over-answering outside the emulated device's scope, not a failure of the feature. Severity kept low for that reason; it would rise to medium if (2) is confirmed for a real target, and the XR_FAILED-masking sub-case is independently worth fixing regardless of (2).

symbol: inline python3 heredoc polling 127.0.0.1:52702 before the OPERATE/OBSERVE loop
what: A python3 heredoc polls 127.0.0.1:52702 up to 60 times and exits 0 (CTRL_UP) / 1 (CTRL_TIMEOUT) to signal Monado control-channel readiness before baseline capture, scenario injection and post-injection capture.
why_meaningless: The heredoc's exit status is never captured (no `RC=$?`, no `||`, no enclosing `if`; the script runs `set -u` only, no `-e`/pipefail), and the printed CTRL_UP/CTRL_TIMEOUT is never grepped. Control falls straight through to line 56, which only tests process liveness, so a timeout changes nothing about the run.
impact: On CTRL_TIMEOUT the script still burns the 6s baseline sleep, injects against an unconfirmed channel, and burns the 5s post sleep before failing at the unrelated PNG-hash assertion (lines 74-91) with no message pointing at the true root cause. Diagnosability cost plus ~11s; the run's verdict itself is still hard-gated.
fix: Capture the heredoc rc (`python3 - <<'PY' ... PY` then `CTRL_RC=$?`) and bail with an explicit 'control channel timeout' message on nonzero, mirroring the APP_DIED check on the next line. While there, fix line 56 as well (see verify_note).
evidence: e2e_playwright_loop.sh:48-55 `python3 - <<'PY' ... print("CTRL_TIMEOUT"); sys.exit(1)` / `PY`, immediately followed by 56: `kill -0 "$APP" 2>/dev/null || { echo APP_DIED; ...; exit 3; }`. No `$?` read between them.
verify_note: The code fact is confirmed — the rc is definitively discarded and CTRL_TIMEOUT is never consulted. But 'meaningless' overstates it, which is why this is PLAUSIBLE not CONFIRMED: the loop's primary job is to BLOCK until the channel is up (it does that correctly), and CTRL_UP/CTRL_TIMEOUT is printed to stdout where the human running this WSL2 bring-up script reads it. There is no green-when-broken path: the terminal assertion (lines 74-91, `ok = len(distinct) >= 2 and bh != ph`, then `exit "$RC"` at 91) is a hard gate, and with the channel down playspectra_server.py cannot change the pose, so frames stay identical and the run fails. Unverified: whether hello_xr under a null Monado compositor could ever produce >=2 distinct frames without injection (a static default pose suggests not, but I did not run it). Stronger adjacent issue found while verifying, which the candidate missed: the liveness check on line 56 is itself near-inert — `APP=$!` is the PID of `timeout`, and in `timeout 40 bash -c "sleep 36 | '$HELLOXR' -g Vulkan2"` the `sleep 36` never writes and so never takes SIGPIPE, keeping the pipeline (and thus `bash -c` and `timeout`) alive for the full 36s even if hello_xr dies instantly. APP_DIED therefore practically cannot fire; a crashed app surfaces as NO_RECDIR (exit 4) instead.

symbol: main() — 'head override moves the located view pose' check
what: After injecting a head pose at (0.6, 1.3, -0.4) the check asserts only that the Euclidean displacement from the pre-injection view pose exceeds 0.3; the landed coordinates are never compared to the injected target.
why_meaningless: Any sufficiently large movement in any direction satisfies moved>0.3, so a wrong-axis or sign-flipped application would still pass this particular assertion.
impact: Limited: a y/z axis swap in the head path would slip past THIS check, but an x-axis regression (wrong axis, sign flip, unapplied target) is caught 20 lines later by the durationMs block, which compares absolutely.
fix: If strengthened, add a per-axis differential rather than a raw absolute compare — e.g. inject two known head positions and assert the difference between the two reported view poses equals the difference of the injected positions (rigid-transform invariant, valid in any reference space).
evidence: scripts/integration_hello_xr.mjs:177-184 — `const p0 = v0.views?.[0]?.pose…; await rpc({cmd:"head",x:0.6,y:1.3,z:-0.4,qw:1}); … const moved = Math.hypot(p1.x-p0.x, p1.y-p0.y, p1.z-p0.z); check("head override moves the located view pose", moved > 0.3, …)`
verify_note: Substantially rebutted. (1) The immediately following durationMs block (lines 191-203) DOES assert absolutely: `Math.abs(pge.x - 2.0) < 0.08` after gliding to x=2.0, so 'moved but landed wrong' on x is caught by the same suite on the same code path — this is exactly the 'looks loose but verified elsewhere' case flagged in the task. (2) The candidate's proposed fix (assert p1 ≈ 0.6/1.3/-0.4) is only conditionally valid: layer/src/hooks_locate.cpp:65 runs the injected head through TransformHeadToSpace() (layer/src/pose_override.cpp:223) from LOCAL into the app's locate space, then RebaseViewsToHead() (pose_override.cpp:206) adds the per-eye IPD offset — so the published y in particular is runtime/space dependent (see memory local-space-origin-per-runtime; the code even logs 'assuming app space == LOCAL … off for STAGE'). A naive absolute assert on y would be a new flake source. Residual gap (why not REJECTED): y/z fidelity of the head path is genuinely unasserted anywhere in this suite. PLAUSIBLE, low.

symbol: main() — 'head override moves the located view pose' check
what: Same displacement-only assertion (delta > 0.5) after injecting a head pose at (0.6, 1.3, -0.4); the landed coordinates are never compared to anything.
why_meaningless: A wrong-but-large movement passes, and unlike the hello_xr suite there is no neighbouring strict check on this path at all.
impact: Head-pose fidelity through the OpenVR→OpenXR translation is unasserted on this path (no durationMs sibling here). Practically bounded: the OpenVR suite is a manual, prerequisite-heavy path, and head injection on it was already only claimed as 'reaches the runtime answer', not 'lands on the commanded coordinate'.
fix: Do NOT assert p1 ≈ the injected coordinates here. Use a space-agnostic strengthening instead: inject two known head positions and assert the delta between the two reported view poses matches the delta of the injected positions (invariant under the LOCAL→STAGE rigid transform), or assert the per-axis sign/ratio of the displacement.
evidence: scripts/integration_openvr.mjs:181-188 — `const p0 = v0.views?.[0]?.pose…; await rpc({cmd:"head",x:0.6,y:1.3,z:-0.4,qw:1}); await sleep(700); … check("head override moves the located view pose", delta > 0.5, …)`
verify_note: The candidate's proposed fix is wrong and I verified why. layer/src/hooks_locate.cpp:63-68 transforms the injected LOCAL-space head into the app's locate space via TransformHeadToSpace (layer/src/pose_override.cpp:223-236) before RebaseViewsToHead; the file's own header comment (integration_openvr.mjs:8) says the OpenComposite path locates in STAGE ('base pose + injection compose in STAGE space'), and pose_override.cpp:229-232 logs that the LOCAL→STAGE transform can be unresolvable. So the reported view pose is deliberately NOT expected to equal the injected numbers on this path — asserting that would manufacture a false red. The underlying observation (nothing verifies WHERE it lands) still stands, so not REJECTED. PLAUSIBLE, low.

what: The `while (Date.now() < deadline)` readiness loop breaks on `st.session && frames > 0`, but on deadline expiry it falls through silently — no throw, no process.exit(1), no 'timed out' branch — and main() then prints status/view/screenshot and resolves normally (exit 0).
why_meaningless: The loop prints a 'waiting: session=… frames=…' progress line that reads like a gate, but a timeout and a success are indistinguishable in the exit code.
impact: run_vrdevapp.sh propagates this rc, so a readiness timeout exits 0. But this is not a green-vs-broken CI gate: vrdevapp_client.mjs contains zero assertions of any kind (no check()/PASS/FAIL anywhere), it is a discovery driver whose output is read by a human, and its rc is only ever nonzero on connect failure/exception. Nothing automated consumes it — scripts/run_all_tests.sh does not call run_vrdevapp.sh, and README.md:71 classifies the VRDevApp path as 🟡 manually verified.
fix: Cheap hardening: after the loop, `if (!(st.session && ((st.capture&&st.capture.framesObserved)||0) > 0)) { console.error('[vrdev] readiness timeout', JSON.stringify(st)); process.exit(1); }` so run_vrdevapp.sh's rc distinguishes timeout from success.
evidence: scripts/vrdevapp_client.mjs:70-79 — loop, then unconditional `console.log("\n[vrdev] status:", JSON.stringify(st))`. scripts/run_vrdevapp.sh:46-49,64 captures `CLIENT_RC=$?` and `exit $CLIENT_RC`.
verify_note: Partially rejected the impact claim. The code fact is certain (silent fall-through, exit 0 on timeout). But 'the app-integration gate goes green' is a misreading: the script asserts nothing at all, so its rc was never a pass/fail signal for anything — the readiness loop's stated intent (comment lines 66-68: 'so we don't screenshot an empty pre-session state') is a best-effort wait, and the timed-out state IS printed (`[vrdev] status: {...session:false...}`) for the human who runs it. Also verified nothing automated calls it: only .claude/settings.json (permission entry), README.md:71 and journal reference run_vrdevapp.sh. PLAUSIBLE (worth the 3-line fix, not a broken gate); severity low.

what: op="eq"/"ne" だけ `actual is not None` ガードが無く、パス誤字 (_resolve→None) かつ value 省略 (=None) の組み合わせで `None == None` → PASS になり得る。
why_meaningless: その組み合わせに限り、検知すべき設定ミス (get パス誤り) が黙って緑になる。
impact: 限定的。repo 内の全シナリオ (tools/scenarios/*.json) は op を near / true しか使っておらず eq は1件も無い。MCP の wait_for は `value: float = 0.0` (tools/playspectra_mcp.py:137) で None が入らない。よって現存する経路で踏むものは無く、手書き JSON / `--cmd` での将来の書き間違いに対する潜在リスク。
fix: ブランケットで `actual is not None` を足すのは非推奨 (eq/null で『フィールドが無い/null』を表明する唯一の手段を潰す)。代わりに assert_state / run_step 側で『op が eq|ne|near|gt|lt のとき value キーが無ければ設定エラーとして FAIL 計上』にするのが安全。
evidence: 361-372 の _cmp: near/gt/lt は `actual is not None and float(...)`、eq/ne は素の `actual == value` / `actual != value`。run_step の assert ラムダ (477-478) は `value=None` 既定。
verify_note: 候補の主張のうち『near/gt/lt との一貫性欠如』という論拠は弱い — float(None) は TypeError を投げ 370-371 の except が拾って False を返すので、near/gt/lt の None ガードは冗長な短絡にすぎず、『None は必ず落とす』という設計方針の証拠にならない。また eq/None は『null であること』を表明する正当な用途にもなり得るため、現状が意図的である可能性を排除できない。未確認: 作者が eq+null 表明を想定していたか (コメント・テスト共に無し。tools/playspectra_math_test.py は lerp3/quat 系のみ、waitfor_test に eq の記述なし＝_cmp の op 別ユニットテストは存在しない)。以上より偽PASS の組み合わせが実在するのは確かだが『意図に反する』の確証は取れず PLAUSIBLE。絶対パス: C:/programing/Arcadia-Metaverses-dev/CluadeDevelopment-VR-App/tools/playspectra_server.py

what: For `srv.wait_for(HZ, "near", 999.0, timeout_ms=350, poll_ms=25)` the elapsed-time assertion accepts 250-1500ms, i.e. up to ~4.3x the configured timeout. The identical band appears in tools/playspectra_capture_assert_test.py:123 against the same 350ms configuration.
why_meaningless: Calling it 'deadline honoured' overstates what is checked: it verifies the call is within a factor of ~4 of its deadline, not that the deadline is honoured. Given the real implementation (playspectra_server.py:374-386, `_poll_until` re-reads time.monotonic() every iteration after probe()), the true expected elapsed is ~350-400ms, so the band leaves ~1.1s of unmonitored slack. A regression that inflates the poll interval (e.g. `time.sleep(poll_ms/100)` instead of `/1000`) would land near 600ms and pass here, and would also pass the neighbouring checks at lines 138-139 and capture_assert_test:115-116 (which only assert `>= 200ms`).
impact: Limited. The check does real work: it catches an ignored/never-armed deadline, ms-vs-seconds unit confusion (350s would blow past 1500ms and fail, just slowly), and any gross overshoot; and the paired `to is False` check on line 146 verifies the semantic outcome independently. The residual gap is a moderate (2-4x) overshoot or a poll-interval inflation in the retry loop that backs every scenario-level `timeout_ms` assertion.
fix: Tighten the upper bound to roughly timeout_ms + a few poll intervals + RTT (e.g. `350 <= el <= 700` here and in capture_assert_test.py:123), or express it relative to the configured values (`timeout_ms <= el <= timeout_ms + 6*poll_ms + 200`) so the band scales if someone edits the timeout. If the wide band is deliberate CI/Windows-scheduler flake margin, say so in a comment so the next reader does not tighten it blindly.
evidence: tools/playspectra_waitfor_test.py:144-147 `to = srv.wait_for(HZ, "near", 999.0, timeout_ms=350, poll_ms=25)` ... `check("timeout deadline honoured (250-1500ms)", 250 <= el <= 1500, ...)`. tools/playspectra_capture_assert_test.py:121-123 duplicates the band with `timeout_ms=350, poll_ms=50`. tools/playspectra_server.py:378-386 shows the deadline is re-evaluated each loop, so a correct implementation overshoots by at most one poll + one probe RTT.
verify_note: Read both test files and _poll_until. This is a tolerance-quality observation, not a defect: I could not establish that the loose bound currently hides anything, and there is a defensible reason for it (these tests run under scripts/run_all_tests.sh:66-67 on Windows, where time.sleep granularity is ~15.6ms and each poll does a localhost socket round-trip to a mock adapter, so a generous ceiling avoids flakes). What is unverified: whether the 1500 ceiling was chosen deliberately as anti-flake margin or arbitrarily — no comment or commit note explains it, and no measured elapsed values are recorded anywhere in the repo to justify the number. PLAUSIBLE rather than CONFIRMED because the assertion is weak, not vacuous.

what: 非CAランタイムで `active` コマンド(InputType::Active)が ApplyFallbackSync 冒頭の `continue` により破棄され、Handle_active は常に ok:true を返す、という指摘。

what: Claim: the haptic telemetry (LayerStateRecordHaptic + Log) is recorded unconditionally BEFORE forwarding, so it cannot distinguish 'the runtime really buzzed' from 'the request was dropped'; and the null-next fallback returns XR_SUCCESS instead of the XR_ERROR_FUNCTION_UNSUPPORTED every sibling hook returns.
why_meaningless: The premise misidentifies the observable. The metric is documented, everywhere it is consumed, as the APP's request (an app-side reaction signal), not as evidence that a physical actuator fired — so recording at the moment of the app's call is precisely the intended semantic, and the runtime's answer is irrelevant to it. The proposed 'fix' (gate the record on XR_SUCCEEDED(r)) would actively break the signal in the exact headless/null-compositor scenario the candidate cites as the risk.
impact: None demonstrable. The grab-detection signal is by construction a measurement of the app under test (the SUT calling xrApplyHapticFeedback), which is exactly the Playwright-analogue observation — like observing that the page called an API, not that a speaker physically made a sound. The null-next XR_SUCCESS branch is a defensive dead path for a mandatory core function; no test or production path can reach it (it would require the app to call the hook with the dispatch table cleared, i.e. after xrDestroyInstance).
fix: No change required for correctness. Optional (cosmetic, low value): add a one-line comment stating the two deliberate choices — (a) the record intentionally precedes the forward because the observable is the app's request, and (b) haptics are best-effort so a missing runtime entry point is reported as XR_SUCCESS rather than failing the app. Do NOT gate LayerStateRecordHaptic on the runtime result: that would convert the only injection-reachability oracle into a false negative on runtimes/drivers with no haptic actuator (the project's own null-compositor Monado path).
evidence: mcp/src/tools/observe.ts:14 — "...and how many haptic pulses the app has requested (an app-side reaction signal)"; observe.ts:103-104 (vr_haptics) — "Return the most recent haptic pulses the app requested (seq, hand, amplitude) — an app-reaction signal (e.g. hello_xr buzzes on grab). Useful to confirm an injected input reached the app."; scripts/integration_hello_xr.mjs:9 — "(c) sync semantics round-trip -> injecting grab>0.9 makes hello_xr buzz -> `haptics` grows", :211 check("sync round-trip: injected grab makes the app buzz"); README.md:57 — "integration_hello_xr の grab→buzz 0→22". Null-next reachability: layer/src/layer_dispatch.cpp:57 resolves applyHapticFeedback via the next xrGetInstanceProcAddr (core OpenXR 1.0 entry point, mandatory for any runtime), and layer/src/layer_entry.cpp:123-132 shows the codebase's explicit policy — only the OPTIONAL xrLocateSpaces hook is gated on `Dispatch().locateSpaces != nullptr`; all core hooks (incl. xrApplyHapticFeedback, layer_entry.cpp:83) are advertised unconditionally because the runtime must provide them.
verify_note: Rejected on documented semantics + consumer code, both of which are unambiguous: the counter is named and described as 'pulses the app requested' in mcp/src/tools/observe.ts:14 and :103-104, and every consumer (scripts/integration_hello_xr.mjs:207-211, scripts/integration_openvr.mjs:194-205 where a missing reaction is an explicit skipCheck, README.md:57) treats it as app-side reaction evidence, never as runtime-actuation evidence. The candidate's own failure scenario ('a driver that never implemented the entry point ... no physical haptic actuator') is the case where its proposed fix would silently destroy the signal — i.e. the fix would introduce the false negative it claims to prevent (this is the 'symptom vs cause' inversion the brief warns about). Residual, genuinely true but inert: the null-next return code differs from the 12 sibling hooks. It is undocumented style inconsistency on an unreachable branch for a core-mandatory function (git log -L214,218 shows the line unchanged since its introduction in bc9bc59cf, only renamed twice), and returning XR_SUCCESS is defensible in fallback mode because the layer itself consumed and recorded the pulse. Not sufficient to sustain the finding's stated impact ('broken but shows green').

what: get_state が hmd.connected をリテラル true で埋めている、という指摘。
why_meaningless: 候補は「set_state の hmd.connected=false は一切読まれない」と主張するが事実誤認。playspectra_proto.c:153 `if (cJSON_IsObject(hmd) && get_flag(hmd, "connected", true))` で確かに読まれており、head 適用のゲートとして機能している(proto_test.c:85-87 「4 disconnected -> present false」で意図がテスト化済み)。さらに定数 true は現時点で常に事実と一致する: builder(target_builder_playspectra.c:77)が HMD xdev を無条件生成し、Monado の static-roles では実行時に xdev を除去できず、制御チャネル自体が HMD/コントローラ device の destroy で停止する(playspectra_controller.c:74-77)。つまりクライアントが get_state を受け取れる全期間で HMD は実在する。候補の fix(state に connected フラグを持たせて echo する)を採ると、OpenXR 側は依然 head pose と view を供給し続けるのに get_state だけが「未接続」と報告する=虚偽報告になり、現状より悪化する。

evidence: playspectra_proto.c:153 `if (cJSON_IsObject(hmd) && get_flag(hmd, "connected", true)) {` — hmd.connected は読まれている。playspectra_proto_test.c:86-87 `parse_str("{\"hmd\":{\"connected\":false}}", &s); CHECK(... && !s.head.present, "4 disconnected -> present false")` — 「connected:false = この device は更新しない」が設計意図として明文テスト済み。target_builder_playspectra.c:77 `struct xrt_device *head = playspectra_hmd_create(&head_center, state);` — HMD は無条件生成・実行時削除経路なし。

impact: None realized. Nothing consumes this script's rc: scripts/run_all_tests.sh (the local CI stand-in) does not invoke it, and the only repo references are a permission entry in .claude/settings.json and a prose comment in scripts/run_hello_xr.sh:18. The core OPERATE proof it demonstrates is separately gated with a hard rc.

If desired as a cosmetic nit, set rc=1 only on hard errors (hello_xr exited early at line 36, or `node inject_client.mjs` nonzero) and keep INCONCLUSIVE at rc=0 to stay consistent with the repo's SKIP policy (review-checklist lens 6: rc is decided by FAIL alone).
